content.user_title: Build React Native Apps with Expo
content.value_statement: Mobile projects need clear guidance for setup, platform differences, and common UI patterns. This skill provides focused React Native and Expo workflows with practical examples.
actual_capabilities: Explains standard commands for starting React Native and Expo development workflows.
Provides a reusable React Native component structure with typed props and styles.
Shows platform-specific rendering and style selection for iOS and Android.
Demonstrates FlatList, TextInput, and loading-state patterns.
Lists accessibility, performance, responsive-design, navigation, and state-management guidance.
Offers troubleshooting steps for Metro, native modules, builds, and simulators.
limitations: It does not create a complete application architecture or backend service.
It does not validate installed dependency versions or local device configuration.
Commands can change project files or install packages when a user chooses to run them.
It provides general guidance and does not replace platform-specific release testing.

use_cases.title: Start an Expo project
use_cases.description: Use the documented workflow to start a development server and install Expo-compatible packages.

use_cases.title: Build cross-platform components
use_cases.description: Apply the component and platform-selection examples when one interface needs iOS and Android support.

use_cases.title: Resolve common development issues
use_cases.description: Follow focused checks for Metro cache failures, native module errors, build configuration, and emulator issues.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic component
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a React Native button component with a title, an onPress handler, accessible labels, and StyleSheet-based styles.

prompt_templates.title: Add platform-specific behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to adjust this React Native screen for iOS and Android using Platform.select. Explain each platform-specific choice.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a list screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my React Native list screen. Recommend FlatList settings, stable keys, accessibility improvements, and ways to reduce unnecessary rendering.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot an Expo build
prompt_templates.prompt: My Expo project fails after adding a native module. Give a safe diagnostic sequence, explain when prebuild is appropriate, and identify files to review.

output: A typed button component using TouchableOpacity and StyleSheet.
Platform-specific spacing and elevation guidance for iOS and Android.
Accessibility labels and roles for screen reader support.

output_examples.input: Metro does not start after a dependency change.
output: A short troubleshooting sequence that checks dependencies and configuration.
Guidance to clear the Expo cache only after reviewing the command impact.
Next steps if the issue continues.

best_practices: Review every command before running it, especially commands that install packages or regenerate native projects.
Test platform-specific changes on both iOS and Android devices or emulators.
Add accessibility labels and roles while building each interactive component.
anti_patterns: Do not use platform-specific APIs without a fallback for the other platform.
Do not use array indexes as list keys when stable item identifiers exist.
Do not run clean or prebuild commands without checking uncommitted project changes.

faq.question: What does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers React Native and Expo setup, components, platform-specific code, common UI patterns, and troubleshooting.

faq.question: Does it support both iOS and Android?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for selecting behavior and styles by platform.

faq.question: Can it install packages?
faq.answer: It documents package installation commands. Review and approve commands before running them in a project.

faq.question: Does it generate native code?
faq.answer: It explains Expo prebuild commands, which generate native project files when you choose to run them.

faq.question: Does it include accessibility guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends accessibility labels and roles for interactive components.

faq.question: Can it fix every build issue?
faq.answer: No. It provides common diagnostic steps, but local dependencies, credentials, and platform tooling can require separate investigation.
